subject: Post-call: Sprint trial orchestration & GPU reservation (trial runway + owners)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Sprint trial orchestration & GPU reservation (trial runway + owners)

Hi Alex — thanks for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into the trial kickoff.

What we heard (success criteria):
- Demo workload: CloudSprint ingest + 8 concurrent user sessions, median latency < 200ms, p95 < 450ms for typical prompts (see sample prompts in the Drive link).
- Quality checks: no more than 8% of responses flagged for hallucination on the baseline test set; automated evals will run nightly.
- Cost target: aim to keep token cost within the budget you mentioned (target $0.015 / 1k tokens average across the trial).

Trial plan & timeline:
- Trial runway: 2 weeks of full-run evaluation starting Monday Nov 22 (testing window 2026-11-22 to 2026-12-05).
- Pre-kickoff: provisioning & baseline benchmark on Nov 18–20 (Redwood to reserve capacity and run smoke tests).
- Mid-point review: Nov 29 quick sync (15 min) to review metrics and adjust burst settings.
- Final readout: Dec 6 evaluation summary and recommended config for production.

Capacity ask (initial):
- Reserved baseline: 2 GPU nodes (A40-equivalent), each provisioned with continuous serving for steady throughput (supporting ~200 rps aggregated).
- Burst / stress window: ability to scale to 6 GPUs for short bursts (minutes to an hour) during load tests and peak replay runs.
- Autoscaling policy: target based on queue depth + p95 latency; soft cap to avoid runaway cost.

Ownership & operational contacts:
- Redwood: Aditya Rao (sales/primary), Monica Patel (solutions/ops lead), Karthik Iyer (SRE — autoscale and infra runbook).
- CloudSprint: Alex Park (technical lead), Jordan Mills (procurement).

Attachments & links:
- capacity_matrix.xlsx (attached) — initial estimate of GPU hours by scenario and cost projection.
- Trial MOP (linked in Drive + will attach updated PDF after we lock config).

Immediate asks for CloudSprint:
1) Confirm the trial window above (Nov 22 start) and procurement timeline for any PO requirements.
2) Confirm success criteria above or add any additional acceptance gates we should instrument.
3) Share an internal contact for network/IP allowlist so we can provision access before baseline tests.

I'll lock the reservation once you confirm; Monica will follow up with the technical runbook and a short pre-kickoff checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this rolling.

Best,
Aditya Rao

- Nov 22 start works for the team (we'll freeze test data and internal signoffs this week).

Looping in some technical details from ops so we can be prescriptive on the reservation and autoscale guardrails. I ran a quick baseline with CloudSprint sample prompts and the numbers below are our recommended starting config: 

Recommended baseline reservation:
- 2x A40-equivalent nodes (continuous serving), 48GB memory each. This covers the steady-state for the 8 concurrent sessions and allows headroom for KV cache.
- Node sizing chosen to optimize for latency at median seq lengths (mostly 256 tokens).

Burst & autoscale plan:
- Burst target: scale up to 6 nodes for load tests and replay slices. Burst windows are expected to be short (5–45 minutes).
- Autoscale policy: scale on (queue depth > 150) OR (p95 latency > 450ms for 3 consecutive 30s windows). Scale steps: +1 node per 30s, cooldown 90s.
- Max spend cap: configure a soft cap that will prevent scaling above 6 nodes unless a named engineering approver overrides during test windows. We'll document escalation flow in the runbook.

Operational runbook (pre-kickoff tasks):
1) Network allowlist: add the IP ranges in the Drive file to your firewall rules (ops@cloudsprint.io).
2) Baseline smoke: Redwood to run 3 smoke test runs (latency + cost) on Nov 18–19 and share logs.
3) Telemetry: instrument p95/p99 latency, token counts, error rates, and avg tokens per response; Redwood will send a link to a live dashboard.
4) Fallback policy: if the primary model fails health checks, traffic will reroute to a lighter variant; we'll notify the team via Slack (ops channel).

I'll attach an updated mini-runbook after we confirm the PO and exact start date. Also answering Alex's question on billing: burst billing is prorated per minute for additional nodes beyond the baseline reservation; baseline reserved capacity is billed hourly as committed usage. We'll include the exact billing table in the trial MOP PDF.

Monica
